GET /IntroSkipper/SupportBundle.classification: expected-extension: IntroSkipper is a compiled-in Ferrofin plugin; stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 lacks it (H=200 vs J=404). By design.

GET /Items/Suggestions.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight pinned full-limit legs (per type, plus a startIndex/TotalRecordCount paging leg). Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. (2) PER-ITEM DTO FIELDS — MediaSources[].Name/Bitrate, MediaStreams[].BitRate (a constant 192000 offset), LocalizedLanguage, Level/IsAVC/Width/Height: the same set already classified on GET /Items/{itemId} as independent-probe noise, inherited here because Suggestions returns full item DTOs. Narrowing the compare to hide either would be the dishonest green; the row stays red until they are fixed on their own rows.

GET /Items/{itemId}/Ancestors.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): with both containers on the same data dir the ancestor rows now align by Path and every field matches except two, BOTH on the UserRootFolder hop. (1) ChildCount J=4 H=3 — UserRootFolder.GetEligibleChildrenForRecursiveChildren (UserRootFolder.cs:96-102) concatenates LibraryManager.RootFolder.VirtualChildren, which is the PlaylistsFolder CreateRootFolder adds at {data}/playlists (LibraryManager.cs:1090-1120); Ferrofin stores that folder parentless and has no AggregateFolder root with virtual children, so the user root counts 3 libraries instead of 4 and /Items?parentId=<root> returns 3. (2) PrimaryImageAspectRatio present on Jellyfin, absent on Ferrofin — FolderImageProvider generates a collage for the user root (Supports() rejects only PhotoAlbum/MusicAlbum and IsTopParent folders); Ferrofin ports CollectionFolderImageProvider (the library tiles) but not FolderImageProvider, so the user root has no Primary image. Un-defer path: port UserRootFolder's virtual-children concat (the direct-children query AND the ChildCount prefetch) and FolderImageProvider. The previous text on this row claimed the residual was '/config-vs-/data path-derived ids only'; that was measurably false — the ids were already identical on both servers and only the Path STRING differed, which is the array align key, so no field was ever compared.

GET /Items/{itemId}/Similar.classification: instance/methodology (RANKED BODY ONLY — status codes, the empty short-circuits, the count invariant and the candidate rule are all still gated, by the reads.py `similar_invariants` probe). Two independent reasons a movie seed's item array cannot diff, both measured on the loop pair. (1) ORDER: Jellyfin 10.11.8 sets `OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, Ascending)]` (v10.11.8 LibraryController.cs:801); five identical calls at limit=12 returned five different SETS, because limit < |universe|. (2) ALGORITHM: 10.11.8 builds ONE flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags }`, while Ferrofin ports upstream master's weighted `MovieSimilarItemsProvider` (genre 10 / tag 5 / studio 5 / director 50 / actor+guest-star 15, MovieSimilarItemsProvider.cs:27-31) plus its phase-2 `IsMovie = true, IsPlayed = false` + ConfigureUserAccess pass. Measured at limit=1000: Jellyfin 299 items, Ferrofin 432, and Jellyfin's set is a STRICT SUBSET of Ferrofin's (onlyJ=0); the 133 extras each share a studio and/or a person with the seed and no genre — master's dimensions exactly. Keeping master is the repo's 'do not port Jellyfin bugs' rule: 10.11.8 additionally over-returns by 4 at every limit (measured 1/3/5/12/50 -> 5/7/9/16/54), because `BaseItemRepository.PrepareFilterQuery` (v10.11.8:1427-1430) adds 4 when `EnableGroupByMetadataKey` and never trims back; Ferrofin honours limit exactly, as master's `.Take(requestedLimit)` does. WHAT IS VERIFIED LIVE instead of a body diff (14 facts, all true on BOTH servers, each computed per server and then compared): status 200, StartIndex 0, TotalRecordCount == len(Items), the seed is never returned, every Type is in the C# IncludeItemTypes, the page is full, len(Items) <= limit+4 (the named Jellyfin quirk is the ONLY slack), an unknown seed is 404 on both, a nil seed is 200-empty on both, an Episode seed short-circuits empty on both, the five aliases agree as sets at limit=1000, and `obeys_own_candidate_rule` — each server's answer is re-derived independently from the DTO fields under ITS OWN documented algorithm (Jellyfin: every row shares a genre or tag with the seed, which 200 of the 500 fixture movies violate; Ferrofin: the answer equals master's weighted model's top-N IN ORDER by score desc then SortName). Negative controls run 2026-08-29: the Ferrofin clause fails on a reversed order and on 12 arbitrary movies, the Jellyfin clause fails on 12 movies outside its universe. Three real Ferrofin bugs this row used to hide were fixed in the same pass: an unknown seed returned 200-empty instead of 404, a nil seed returned 400 instead of the C# root-folder fallback, and the no-limit default was 10 instead of C#'s `limit ?? 50` (SimilarItemsManager.cs:93).

GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. The scorer half is fixed — the seed's kind now selects the C# provider shape (`MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider` is a flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [MusicArtist] }`, and an EMPTY Genres/Tags pair is not a predicate, so an untagged artist must match every other artist; covered by the `an_untagged_artist_seed_still_matches_every_other_artist` unit test). What still blocks it is the item-UNIVERSE divergence, not the similarity code: Ferrofin materializes MusicArtist as a parentless by-name row with a NULL TopParentId, and every user-scoped `InternalItemsQuery` is scoped to the user's views via `TopParentId IS NOT NULL` (item_repository.rs `scope_to_user_libraries`, the port of C# `AddUserToQuery`), so no artist is reachable by any query that does not name it by id. Detector, both servers: `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=MusicArtist` -> F 0, J 3, while `/Artists?userId=<u>` returns all 3 on both, and adding `&ids=<artistId>` makes the same query return the row on Ferrofin. Same root cause as the MusicArtist/Folder/TvChannel/UserView rows missing from GET /Items/Suggestions. Un-defer path: give the MusicArtist by-name row a TopParentId (Jellyfin's artist rows are physical folder items under the music library, which is why they survive `AddUserToQuery`) — this changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it needs its own change with the perf gate, not a ride-along.

POST /Packages/Installed/{name}.classification: accepted-divergence: repository install of WASM plugins is real (2026-08-14: ABI gate → HTTPS-per-hop download → streamed size cap → sha256/md5 verify → component+identity validation → guid-squat refusal → atomic stage → restart-required; admin-only; end-to-end server test). Divergence vs Jellyfin: the install is SYNCHRONOUS — none of the PackageInstalling/Completed/Failed/Cancelled WebSocket messages are emitted (no dashboard progress; a slow repo holds the POST open), and the plugin appears in /Plugins only after the activating restart. Async install + Package* push is the recorded follow-up (WebSocket-push backlog).

DELETE /Packages/Installing/{packageId}.classification: accepted-divergence: always 404 — installs are synchronous, so no tracked installation exists to cancel (Jellyfin tracks async installs). Admin-only.

GET /web/ConfigurationPage.classification: expected-extension: compiled-in/extension route not on the stock Jellyfin surface the fixture exercises.

POST /Startup/User.classification: accepted-divergence: post-setup the first user already has a password and the contract is 403 (the Forbid guard upstream added in v12, ported by Ferrofin); Jellyfin 10.11.8 predates it and answers 204, silently re-setting the admin password. The journey asserts the correct contract (H=403 J=204).

GET /Trailers.classification: instance: Jellyfin 10.11.8 returns 500 here (its own error with no Trailers provider), while Ferrofin correctly returns 200 with an empty result. Kept correct per policy (do not port Jellyfin bugs); not a Ferrofin gap.

POST /MergeVersions/MergeMovies.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin ships the MergeVersions controller (danieladov 'Merge Versions' plugin surface) compiled-in; stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 lacks it (H=2xx vs J=404). By design.

POST /MergeVersions/MergeEpisodes.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin ships the MergeVersions controller compiled-in; stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 lacks it (H=2xx vs J=404). By design.

POST /MergeVersions/SplitMovies.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin ships the MergeVersions controller compiled-in; stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 lacks it (H=2xx vs J=404). By design.

POST /MergeVersions/SplitEpisodes.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin ships the MergeVersions controller compiled-in; stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 lacks it (H=2xx vs J=404). By design.

GET /Years/{year}.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin does not materialize Year items (documented out-of-scope; matches the GET /Years classification), so a single year has no item to return (H=404 vs J=200).

GET /Playlists/{itemId}/InstantMix.classification: expected-extension: Ferrofin generates an instant mix for a playlist (H=200); stock Jellyfin returns 404 (playlists are not an instant-mix source). A harmless superset.

GET /Studios/{name}.classification: accepted-divergence: Ferrofin does not lazily CREATE a by-name item on a GET (Jellyfin's GetItemByName writes a row as a read side-effect → J=200 for an absent studio). Ferrofin returns the item if it exists (200, BaseItemDto) else 404 — a GET with no filesystem write. Verified live 2026-08-11: existing→200, absent→404.

GET /Genres/{genreName}.classification: accepted-divergence: same no-lazy-create-on-GET family as /Studios/{name}. Existing genre→200 BaseItemDto (both servers), absent→Ferrofin 404 vs Jellyfin auto-created 200. Shape verified.

GET /Persons/{name}.classification: accepted-divergence: same no-lazy-create-on-GET family as /Studios/{name}. Existing person→200 BaseItemDto, absent→404 (both servers 404 in the harness run). Shape verified.

GET /Genres.classification: verified 2026-08-11: QueryResult<BaseItemDto> (Items array + TotalRecordCount + StartIndex), status+schema conformant; empty-library returns the well-formed empty result.

GET /MusicGenres.classification: verified 2026-08-11: QueryResult<BaseItemDto>, status+schema conformant (same by-name list shape as /Genres).

GET /LiveTv/Timers/Defaults.classification: verified 2026-08-11: SeriesTimerInfoDto defaults (ChannelId/Days/padding flags/…), 200 + schema conformant.

GET /DisplayPreferences/{displayPreferen.classification: verified 2026-08-11: the auto-flag was a harness artifact (literal unresolved {displayPreferencesId}); with a real client key (e.g. usersettings?client=emby) Ferrofin returns 200 DisplayPreferencesDto (Id/Client/SortBy/CustomPrefs) — the by-client resolution Jellyfin uses.
